text: Course 6's capstone built a real scoped application for tracking employee equipment loans. An employee requests equipment, their manager approves it, and a before-insert Business Rule calls the EquipmentAvailabilityChecker Script Include to block a duplicate request. That whole chain is the application's critical path — the one sequence that absolutely has to keep working through every future change.

The UI Test impersonates the employee first: open the request form, pick an available piece of equipment, submit, and verify the new record is now Pending Approval. Then it impersonates the manager: open that same request, change its state to Approved, submit, and verify the state actually changed.

That ten-step sequence is a single UI Test, but it exercises the entire employee-to-manager handoff through the real UI Policies and field-level ACLs each role would actually encounter — not just as an admin clicking through both forms as the same account.

The UI Test confirms the experience works, but says nothing directly about the Script Include's own logic. A server-side Test creates a Checked Out request against a specific piece of equipment, calls isEquipmentAvailable against that same equipment, and verifies the method returns false.

Grouped into one Test Suite named Equipment Checkout Regression, both Tests report a single combined result for the whole critical path. Scheduled to run nightly, that Suite runs every night with nobody involved, and surfaces a future regression as a failed Test the very next run.

This lab used every mechanism this chapter introduced, in the order it introduced them — Test Steps, a UI Test with real roles, a server-side Test validating logic directly, and both grouped into a scheduled Suite. That's the complete pattern for any application on this platform. Next up: Chapter 5 opens with the ServiceNow DevOps app, and where ATF fits into a real CI/CD pipeline.
